sentences.text: this appeal challenging the award passed by Principal Special Judge, Special Court under EC and NDPS Act, Chennai in M.A.C.T.O.P.No.5399 of 2014 dated 14.03.2018.

2. The case of the claimant is that he was riding a two wheeler on 11.07.2014 near Vadapalani bus depot and at about 6.40 hours, the bus belonging to the Transport Corporation was driven in a rash and negligent manner.
As a result of which, the bus dashed on the two wheeler and the claimant was thrown out of the two wheeler and he sustained the following injuries and disability:-

1. Grade III A compound communited Fracture Lateral tibial condule left knee 2. Tibia with head of fibula fracture left leg.
3. Laceration over left knee 10*4*2* cm
Pain and stiffness left knee and movement.

Restricted IP and ER with knee flexion 45 only (Normal 0-35), Difficulty in walking climbing steps,
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1208 of 2024 sitting cross legged and squatting.
Disfiguration over left knee.
Difficulty in active standing work.
Mal united fracture.
3. The claimant under went treatment as an in patient in phases for nearly four months and he took treatment for over a period of 10 months.
The doctor who had treated the claimant issued a disability certificate showing that the claimant suffered 45% partial and permanent disability.
It is under these circumstances, the claim petition came to be filed seeking for payment of compensation by the transport corporation.

4. The Tribunal on considering the facts and circumstances of the case and on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence came to a conclusion that the accident had taken place only due to the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the bus belonging to the Transport Corporation.

5. Having rendered such a finding, the Tribunal proceeded to https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1208 of 2024 fix the compensation and the total compensation was fixed at Rs.2,01,000/- under various heads as follows :-

Sl . Compensation awarded under Amount No. the head (in Rs.)
1. Loss of earning 30,000/-

2. Transport to hospital and Extra 10,000/- Nourishment 3. Damages to clothing and purchase - of medicines 4. Cost of treatment and purchase of 1,000/- medicines 5. Loss of income to the family 10,000/- members of the petitioner Imam @ Imamsa vs The Managing Director on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39930320/
2 6. Loss of amenities - 7. Pain and suffering 30,000/-
8. Petitioners permanent disability 1,20,000/-
9. Loss of earning power -- Total Rs.2, 01,000/-

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The above compensation was directed to be paid with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.
6. The claimant not being satisfied with the quantum of compensation fixed by the Tribunal has filed this appeal seeking for enhancement of compensation.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1208 of 2024

7. Heard Mr.K.V.Muthu Vasan, learned counsel for appellant/claimant and M/s.M.Murali Vinoth,
learned counsel for respondent.
8. This Court carefully considered the submissions made on either side and the materials available on record.
9. This Court also carefully went through the award passed by the Tribunal.
10. The Tribunal has fixed Rs.3,000/- per percentage by quantifying the total disability percentage at 40%.

The accident had taken place on 11.07.2014 and taking into consideration the judgement of the Division Bench in CMA No.3334 of 2021 dated 15.06.2022, this Court is inclined to fix a sum of Rs.5,000/- per percentage.

Thus, the compensation under the head of disability is fixed at Rs.2,00,000/- (5,000 x 40%).
11.
The claimant in this case claimed to be a Tailor and was aged https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.1208 of 2024 about 51 years.
The injuries that were sustained by the claimant and the consequence of such injuries shows that fracture was suffered in both the legs.
The claimant had also taken treatment as an in patient for nearly four months.
It can therefore be safely concluded that the claimant would have been out of action for atleast 10 months.
The notional income of the claimant can be fixed at Rs.10,000/- per month.
Thus, the compensation under the head of loss of earnings can be fixed at Rs.1,00,000/- (10,000 x 10 months).

12. Considering the nature of the injuries and the treatment undergone by the claimant, the compensation under the head of transport to hospital and extra nourishment can be enhanced to Rs.50,000/- and the compensation under the head of attendar charges can be enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
Under the head of damages to clothing and articles, a sum of Rs.1,500/- can be fixed.
